title: NSE Holidays 2026: NSE and BSE Share Market Holiday List
summary: NSE holidays 2026, BSE holidays and the next share market holiday. Full trading calendar, Muhurat session date and which F&O expiries shift.
body_markdown:
*Calendar checked on 15 September 2026. Covers equity and equity derivatives. Other segments may follow different schedules, outlined below.*


The next scheduled share market holiday is Friday, 2 October 2026, for Mahatma Gandhi Jayanti. NSE and BSE close for equity and F&O trading, with regular trading scheduled to resume on Monday, 5 October.


The NSE holidays 2026 calendar lists 16 weekday closures, including the 15 January Maharashtra municipal election holiday. Four listed occasions fall on weekends and are shown separately. Muhurat trading is scheduled for Sunday, 8 November 2026, with timings to be notified separately.

The[BSE holiday page](https://www.bseindia.com/static/markets/marketinfo/listholi) carries segment-specific calendars. Select your segment before relying on a date.

## Muhurat Trading 2026


### Date: Sunday, 8 November 2026. Timings: to be notified by exchange circular.


Muhurat trading is a special session on Diwali Laxmi Pujan marking the start of the new Samvat year. It runs despite 8 November being both a Sunday and a listed trading holiday.


It is a live session with real price discovery and execution. Even a small token order is subject to normal matching and liquidity conditions; submitting it does not guarantee a fill.


Confirm the 2026 circular and your broker's participation before setting order timings.


Note that **Tuesday, 10 November** is a separate weekday holiday for Diwali-Balipratipada.


## Holidays by Segment


The equity list is not the whole calendar.


-


**Equity and equity derivatives:** the 16 weekday closures above.


-


**NSE currency derivatives:** the equity holidays plus four additional weekday closures: **19 February, 19 March, 1 April and 26 August 2026** . These cover Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Jayanti, Gudi Padwa, annual bank closing and Id-E-Milad, respectively.


-


**Commodity derivatives:** trading splits into morning and evening sessions. On some holidays only the morning session closes while the evening session trades. Check the specific date.


Check out[BANKEX Expiry 2026: Day, Dates & Lot Size](https://algotest.in/blog/bankex-expiry/)


## Trading Holiday vs Settlement Holiday vs Bank Holiday


Type


What changes


What to check


Trading holiday


Trading is closed in the affected segment


Next session, any expiry shift


Settlement holiday


Trading may be open, but settlement is not processed


Delivery dates, availability of sale proceeds


Bank holiday


Banking services affected; does not close the market by itself


Your bank, broker funding, exchange calendar


If you sell shares near a holiday, check the settlement schedule before assuming proceeds are withdrawable on a given date.


**SIP instalments:** check the fund's business-day calendar and applicable cut-off rules. The NAV depends on when the transaction and funds meet those rules, so the next business day's NAV is not automatic.


Related:[Nifty Expiry Day: 7 Rules Every Options Trader Should Follow (2026)](https://algotest.in/blog/nifty-expiry-day/)


## What Happens If an F&O Expiry Falls on a Holiday?


NSE holidays 2026, BSE holidays and the next share market holiday. Full trading calendar, Muhurat session date and which F&O expiries shift.


For[Nifty weekly and monthly options](https://algotest.in/blog/nifty-expiry-day/) , an expiry that falls on a trading holiday moves to the **previous trading day** .


For example, **Tuesday, 20 October 2026 is Dussehra** , so that week’s Nifty expiry would move to **Monday, 19 October** under the current rules. Check the expiry date displayed for your contract before placing a trade.


This matters if your strategy trades on a fixed weekday. A Tuesday-only entry rule could miss the Monday expiry. When[backtesting your options strategy](https://algotest.in/blog/how-to-backtest-options-trading-strategies-with-examples/) , look at past holiday weeks and check when the strategy actually entered and exited.


If you plan to keep positions open through the holiday, review your position size and available margin. These[risk management checks](https://algotest.in/blog/trading-risk-management-rules-examples-and-a-practical-plan/) matter because you cannot exit while the market is closed.


## Conclusion


Check the calendar for the segment you trade rather than the equity list alone, and confirm the listed contract when a holiday lands near expiry. Review your entry and exit rules against the revised dates before deploying a strategy.
